name: @kickside/renderers-ui
title: KickSide Content Renderers
description: Isolated, reusable content-viewer web components for kickside. Each viewer (markdown, pdf, image) is its own lazy-loaded bundle so heavy deps (pdfjs, markdown-it, highlight.js) never enter a host bundle. <wc-resource-view> is the reusable host: given a content-type + source it mounts the matching viewer by tag. Used by the wiki, uploads, inbox, anywhere.

wippy.description: Content-viewer web component set for kickside: <wc-resource-view> is the reusable host this wippy block describes, and each viewer (markdown, code, HTML, image, PDF, audio, video, Word docx, Excel xlsx, PowerPoint pptx) ships as its own lazy-loaded bundle so heavy deps like pdfjs, markdown-it, highlight.js, docx-preview, and xlsx never enter a host bundle. Pass the resource via attributes: content-type (MIME type), source (inline text), source-url (URL to fetch bytes/text from), plus optional alt for images and filename so viewers can infer type from the extension. The host fetches renderer descriptors from GET /api/v1/renderers (kickside.renderer registry entries declaring tag, content_types, and priority), picks the best match (exact type beats type/* prefix beats */* wildcard, then highest priority), lazy-loads that viewer by tag via loadByTagName, and forwards all attributes to it. If the registry call fails it falls back to a built-in pdf/image/markdown table, unknown or empty text types fall back to the markdown viewer, and a completely unmatched type shows a no-inline-viewer notice with an Open link when source-url is set. It emits no custom events; adding a new viewer is registry-only (register a descriptor plus ship its bundle, no host change needed).

source-url.description: URL to fetch the resource from.

filename.description: Original filename, forwarded to viewers that infer type from the extension.
